Definition: Integration of company registration, business licensing, tax compliance, regulatory compliance data
Comments: The e-business pillar (pillar 3 of Congo Digital 2025) targets private sector digital services. The PATN project includes 57 projects including business environment improvements. No documented operational integration of business registry with a data exchange platform.
revision_notes: Score of 2 (Planned) confirmed. World Bank PAD (2022) and UNDP blog document PATN/Congo Digital strategy plans for an e-business pillar and business environment reform, but no evidence of operational data exchange integration with company registration or licensing systems. A June 2026 UNECA assessment of Congo's data governance ecosystem confirms interoperability frameworks remain limited and no integrated data-sharing platform exists across sectors, consistent with the current score. No fresher sector-specific source was found for business registration, so the original score stands.
revised_comments: The e-business pillar of the Congo Digital strategy targets improvements to the business environment, including company registration and licensing reform, under the World Bank-financed Digital Acceleration Project (PATN) and related business environment initiatives. Business registration and licensing systems are not yet integrated into an operational government data exchange platform; integration remains at the planning stage pending development of the national interoperability framework.

Definition: Extent to which the national digital identity system is integrated with the data exchange for identity verification and authentication
Comments: No operational national digital ID system that is integrated with data exchange. The digital transformation project includes foundational digital identity as planned component. No evidence of functional integration.
revision_notes: Score of 2 (Planned) confirmed and refreshed. EIB and World Bank project documents confirm a national interoperability/data exchange framework was still being defined as of 2022-2023. A July 2025 TechAfrica News report confirms Congo held a national workshop in Brazzaville to develop a roadmap for a digital identity system under PATN, backed by the World Bank, CARIA and Thales, explicitly aiming for future interoperability across institutions - confirming that as of mid-2025 no operational digital ID-to-data-exchange integration exists and the system remains at the roadmap/planning stage. Score unchanged but evidence updated to 2025.
revised_comments: Congo does not yet have an operational national digital identity system integrated with a government data exchange platform. A national workshop held in Brazzaville in July 2025, convened under the PATN digital transformation project with World Bank financing and technical support from partners including Thales, is developing a roadmap for a secure, interoperable digital identity system. Digital ID integration into data exchange therefore remains at the planning stage.

Definition: Integration of learner records, academic credentials, enrollment data, and scholarship/bursary systems
Comments: The EIB/EU project explicitly targets priority IT systems in tertiary education. The project will 'develop and implement systems targeting tertiary education.' Under development as part of the broader digital transformation project.
revision_notes: Score revised upward from 2 (Planned) to 3 (Under development). The EIB-financed component of the Congo Digital Transformation project explicitly targets development and implementation of priority IT systems in tertiary education. An EIB press release (24 June 2025) confirms the EU-funded phase of PATN, which includes enhancing data management in higher education, began operational deployment in November 2024. TechAfrica News (23 June 2025) confirms deployment is under way. This constitutes active implementation rather than a merely planned intervention, warranting an upgrade to Under development. There is no evidence yet that the education system is integrated into a live, cross-government data exchange platform, so Partially integrated (4) is not yet supported.
revised_comments: Development of priority IT systems for the tertiary education sector is under active implementation as part of the EU/EIB-financed component of Congo's PATN digital transformation project, which began operational deployment in November 2024. The work focuses on strengthening data management in higher education as part of the broader national interoperability framework, though the education sector is not yet integrated into an operational, cross-government data exchange platform.

Definition: Integration of tax administration and revenue collection systems data into the exchange platform
Comments: The digital transformation project targets priority IT systems. Tax digitalization is a goal of e-government reform under PATN. No documented operational integration of tax systems with the interoperability platform yet.
revision_notes: Score of 2 (Planned) confirmed. The EIB/EU project scope (education, health, cybersecurity, CERT, interoperability framework) does not list tax and revenue systems among its priority sectoral integrations, and the World Bank PAD explicitly notes tax collection back-office systems were developed independently by line ministries with limited interoperability and scalability potential. Congo has operated a standalone biometric Tax ID Card system since 2020 (Ministry of Finance, developed with Muhlbauer) with third-party interfaces to customs and banks, but there is no evidence this legacy system has been integrated into the national interoperability/data exchange platform now under development. Score therefore remains Planned rather than Under development.
revised_comments: Congo operates a standalone biometric Tax ID Card system, in place since 2020, run by the Ministry of Finance and Budget, which supports third-party data exchange with customs and banking institutions for KYC and revenue verification purposes. This system has not yet been integrated into the national government data exchange platform currently being developed under the PATN/Congo Digital transformation programme; integration remains at the planning stage.

Definition: Whether a detailed implementation roadmap with phases, milestones, and timelines exists for data exchange development
Comments: The PATN (Digital Transformation Acceleration Project) launched January 2023 implements 57 projects for 2024 within the broader framework. A clear roadmap is under development as part of the World Bank project conditions. World Bank explicitly noted that 'implementation must follow suit' and a 'clear and prioritized roadmap' is needed.
revision_notes: Score revised upward from 2 (Under development) to 3 (Yes). At appraisal (2022) the World Bank explicitly noted the absence of a clear and prioritised roadmap for the Vision Congo Digital 2025 strategy. By mid-2025, however, the PATN implementation roadmap is concretely documented: binding financing and grant agreements dated 30 December 2022, 30 December 2023 and 2 September 2024, EU-funded operational deployment beginning November 2024 over a defined five-year horizon, and specific sectoral milestones covering education, health, cybersecurity, CERT, interoperability framework and data protection. TechAfrica News (23 June 2025) and the EIB press release (24 June 2025) confirm this phased implementation is publicly documented and under way, meeting the threshold for a published implementation roadmap.
revised_comments: A phased implementation roadmap for Congo's digital transformation programme (PATN) is publicly documented, comprising World Bank, EIB and EU financing tranches signed between December 2022 and September 2024, with operational deployment of the EU-funded component beginning in November 2024 over a five-year horizon. The roadmap sets out specific milestones across sectors including higher education, health, cybersecurity, data protection and the interoperability and data exchange framework.

Definition: Whether a formal strategy or policy document exists specifically for government data exchange and interoperability
Comments: 'Vision Congo Digital 2025' strategy adopted, with e-government as pillar 2. The NDP 2022-2026 commits to digital economy as priority. Interoperability framework included in the multi-donor PATN project. No standalone comprehensive data exchange strategy; it is embedded within the broader digital strategy.
revision_notes: Score of 2 (Mentioned in Broader DPI/Digital Strategy) confirmed. Congo's original Vision Congo Digital 2025 has been succeeded by the Congo Digital 2030 plan (cited in the EIB's June 2025 press release), which references e-government, e-citizen and e-commerce pillars including a future interoperability and data exchange framework, but remains a broad digital-economy strategy rather than a standalone data exchange or interoperability strategy. This is corroborated by a June 2026 UNECA country assessment, which explicitly finds the absence of an integrated national data governance strategy and limited interoperability frameworks in Congo, and which is now supporting the government in developing a dedicated National Data Governance Strategy. Score therefore remains at 2 pending adoption of that standalone strategy.
revised_comments: Government data exchange and interoperability objectives are referenced within Congo's broader digital economy strategy (Congo Digital 2030, successor to Vision Congo Digital 2025) and the associated PATN transformation programme, rather than in a dedicated, standalone data exchange or interoperability strategy. A National Data Governance Strategy is under development with UNECA and GIZ support, following a 2026 country assessment that identified the absence of an integrated data governance framework as a key gap.

Definition: Current operational status of the data exchange system
Comments: An IT interoperability framework and data exchange platform is being defined and implemented as part of the EIB/EU/World Bank Congo Digital Transformation project (€136.5M total). The EIB project explicitly includes 'definition of an IT interoperability framework and data exchange platform.' The World Bank component (PATN, launched Jan 2023) has 57 projects for 2024. Platform under active development but not yet fully operational across government.
revision_notes: Score of 3 (Under Development) confirmed. The EU/EIB-funded phase of PATN, targeting the IT interoperability framework and data exchange platform among other components, began operational deployment in November 2024 (confirmed by EIB press release and TechAfrica News, both June 2025). However, a June 2026 UNECA country assessment, following consultations with 21 institutions, explicitly finds limited interoperability frameworks and fragmented institutional data-sharing arrangements still in place, indicating the exchange platform is not yet operational. Score remains Under Development rather than Partially or Fully Operational.
revised_comments: Congo is actively developing a government data exchange and interoperability platform as part of the World Bank, EIB and EU-financed PATN digital transformation programme, whose EU-funded component began operational deployment in November 2024. A 2026 UNECA assessment of the country's data governance ecosystem confirms that interoperability frameworks remain limited and that an integrated cross-government data exchange system is not yet operational, with a National Data Governance Strategy now under development to address these gaps.

Definition: Extent to which provincial/state and local governments participate in the data exchange
Comments: The digital transformation is led by central government through MPTEN. The World Bank project targets national-level public sector capacity. No documented sub-national (departmental/municipal) participation in data exchange.
revision_notes: Score of 1 (National level only) confirmed. The World Bank PAD and June 2026 UNECA workshops describe stakeholder engagement limited to central government ministries, regulatory agencies, academia, private sector and development partners (21 institutions consulted); no departmental or municipal government participation in data exchange design or governance is documented. No evidence found of sub-national government involvement in Congo's data exchange initiative.
revised_comments: Congo's data exchange and interoperability initiative is coordinated and implemented at the central government level, led by the Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and the Digital Economy together with national regulatory and cybersecurity agencies. No evidence indicates the involvement of provincial or municipal authorities in the design, governance or use of the data exchange platform.
